title: I Posted the Condo Bike-Room Camera After My Lock Walked

parts.text: I opened the bike room at 6:48 a.m. and my U-lock was on a different frame. My bike was gone. The board had said cameras were coming, then said privacy, then said maybe. I was thirty-six, commuter, holding an empty wall hook. A notice on the door still promised 24/7 recording. I photographed the notice, the foreign lock, the hook. Then I posted both in the resident portal under Lost Property, not Accusations. At 6:55 a board member replied that posting camera talk was inflammatory. The notice was their letterhead.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: They called their own camera notice inflammatory while my hook is empty.

social.video_title: The U-lock stayed; the bike did not — Part 1/2
social.description: Empty hook, promised cameras, letterhead notice. Portal said inflammatory. Would you have used Accusations?

parts.text: Building ops admitted a camera existed and had a clip of a resident using a spare fob. The bike came back from a storage cage that was not his. The board replaced the notice with an actual live URL for residents. I bought a new lock anyway. Inflammatory is a word for when letterhead meets a hook. I commute again. The cage has a name on it now. Names help.

social.video_title: The clip went to a cage that was not his — Part 2/2
social.description: Bike returned, live URL, new lock. Was privacy a spare fob?
